sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, Vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 461-526. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Family-level only. p. 477: 'In their phonologies, the East-Central Family languages show a strong development of supra-segmental features manifesting themselves in tonal systems and combined tone-stress systems.' Keiagana appears only in the census list (p. 469, Kamano Sub-Family, 8,000 speakers) and in fn. 4 on Kamano dialect intelligibility chains; the chapter gives illustrative phonology notes for Yagaria (cross-ref to (III)7.5.3), Kuman, Awa etc., never for Keyagana. No stress-placement statement for Keyagana.
